acceptance: Root LICENSE matches the canonical Apache License 2.0 text by documented SHA-256 digest and the repository identifies Apache-2.0 as the license for Kernux-owned code.

A canonical license policy states that Apache-2.0 covers Kernux-owned code only and does not erase or replace third-party license, attribution, trademark, asset, model/data, binary, or service obligations.

Compatibility evidence records MIT for the three pinned public founding-donor references, MIT/Apache-2.0 for the current installed JavaScript toolchain/support packages, and no external Cargo dependency.
The policy allows current MIT/Apache-2.0 inputs subject to preserved notices and requires explicit review before any other license class enters a distributed Kernux artifact.

Project-license validation rejects missing/tampered/symlinked LICENSE or policy files, loss of third-party boundary language, a non-private root npm package, or a non-virtual root Cargo manifest without an intentional governed policy update.
The policy requires every future distributable npm package or Rust crate to declare explicit SPDX license metadata before release.
The WorkPacket binds exact canonical evidence that KX-P00-S04-T02 is already PROVEN; no native SpecGrain lifecycle state is fabricated.

Exact implementation passes focused license-policy tests, existing provenance/notice validation, baseline CI, Diffcipline R2 PASS on the exact change, OpenCodeReview on supported changed files, and post-merge main qualification.

minimality.rationale: Reuse the existing Python provenance enforcement and standard-library parsers; add no runtime/development dependency solely to enforce the license contract.

requirements: Do not invent a legal copyright owner, CLA, patent owner, or trademark grant.
Do not treat repository-level Apache-2.0 as relicensing third-party material; preserved upstream terms remain authoritative for that material.
Do not silently classify copyleft, proprietary, custom, model/data, trademark, binary, or hosted-service terms as compatible based only on SPDX labels.
Do not fetch mutable network license text at validation time; validation must be reproducible from repository-owned evidence and canonical pinned digest/text.
Do not add distributable-package metadata to private/virtual roots merely to satisfy a project-license task.
Do not manually mutate SpecGrain lifecycle state to manufacture dependency eligibility.

outcome: Kernux-owned code is explicitly licensed under Apache-2.0 with deterministic repository validation, preserved third-party license boundaries, and a conservative compatibility policy for current donors/dependencies and future distributable packages.
rationale: KX-P00-S04-T02 is canonically proven. The repository still has no project LICENSE. Apache-2.0 preserves permissive adoption while adding an explicit patent grant. Current public founding-donor references are MIT, the installed JavaScript toolchain resolves only MIT/Apache-2.0 licenses, and Cargo currently has no external dependencies. The root npm package is private and the Cargo root is a virtual workspace, so this task applies the repository license now without introducing publish metadata into non-distributable roots; future publishable packages/crates must declare SPDX metadata before release.

risk.recovery: Revert the bounded project-license/policy changes before a release that depends on them; the task imports no donor product code and creates no product/user runtime state.

scope_in: Apply the exact Apache License 2.0 text from the Apache Software Foundation as the repository-root LICENSE for Kernux-owned code.
Document a canonical license policy distinguishing Kernux-owned code from donor code, dependencies, assets, model/data artifacts, trademarks, generated material, binaries, and hosted services.

Record an evidence-backed compatibility posture for the three pinned founding public donor references, the exact currently installed JavaScript license inventory, and the dependency-free Rust workspace.

Implement dependency-free validation that fails closed when LICENSE bytes, canonical policy identity, private npm-root status, virtual Cargo-root status, or required third-party boundary language drifts.
Require future distributable npm packages or Rust crates to declare explicit SPDX license metadata before release; do not add publish metadata to the current private/virtual roots.
Integrate project-license validation into existing CI/provenance enforcement and document the review path for future dependency or donor license classes.

Bind the already-proven KX-P00-S04-T02 prerequisite through exact canonical CURRENT/tasks/T02 evidence in the WorkPacket because the pinned SpecGrain lifecycle exposes no supported post-Grain state-mutation command.
scope_out: No donor product source import and no relicensing of any third-party code, license snapshot, asset, model weight, trademark, binary, or hosted service.
No CLA/DCO/contributor-governance policy; KX-P00-S01-T03 remains separate.
No release SBOM, generated release NOTICE bundle, installer attribution packaging, package publication, or full transitive legal-opinion automation.

No assertion that Apache-2.0 resolves every future license combination; weak-copyleft, copyleft, network-copyleft, proprietary, custom, dual-license, asset/model/data, or ambiguous terms require explicit review before admission.
title: KX-P00-S01-T04 — Establish Apache-2.0 project license and compatibility policy
